rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (base_speed 1.0, kd 0.30, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, sensors at ±0.05 m with 16 mm footprints, search_left) is the best raced design at 85.60. Iteration 9 reproduced it exactly, so the result is stable. Oval progress is 0.3425 with 0 line losses. Oval max_error is about 0.062, just over the 0.06 m limit. Each of s-bend and slalom still loses the line once per run. Across iterations 5 to 6, cutting speed from 1.4 to 1.2 to 1.0 raised oval progress (0.137, 0.318, 0.3425), and the gain is flattening. Iteration 7 (kd 0.20) and iteration 8 (±0.08 m spread) both hurt, so damping and sensing span should stay fixed.

Change: base_speed from 1.0 to 0.9, with every other field at its iteration 6 value. This is the one lever with a consistent trend that has not yet been tested. Lower entry speed should reduce oval peak error, so the expected result is oval progress near or above 0.34 and oval max_error below 0.06. The risk is that progress falls if 0.9 is too slow. Iteration 6 stays as the fallback, and it can be re-approved if this race is worse.

Hypotheses: (a) base_speed 0.9 keeps oval progress at or above about 0.33 with 0 oval line losses; (b) oval max_error falls below 0.06 on more seeds; (c) s-bend and slalom remain at about 0.16 and 0.11 progress with 1 line loss each, since speed is not their limit. Measurements requested: all, with focus on oval progress and max_error, and on s-bend and slalom line-loss events.
